item.title: Tech-Utopian Movement Praxis Says It Has Found a Home in Uruguay
item.description: After a sprawling world tour, Praxis, a New York-based, crypto-backed “digital nation,” has signed a deal to build a physical city in Uruguay.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola and Sarah Pabst
item.media:description: Construction of apartment buildings as part of the +Colonia city development in Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay. Praxis said it plans to build its community within +Colonia.

item.title: Paris Really, Really Loves Céline Dion
item.description: Ms. Dion, the French Canadian diva, has embarked on her first solo tour of France since the pandemic. The French are swooning.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Porter, Giulia Imbert and Dmitry Kostyukov

item.title: Takeaways From Charles Spencer’s Memoir, “Swan Song,” About Princess Diana
item.description: Nearly 30 years after Princess Diana died, her brother has written a book about her life, her marriage to Prince Charles and the suffering she endured at the hands of the tabloid press.
item.dc:creator: The Book Review

item.title: British Columbia Sues OpenAI Over Tumbler Ridge Shooting
item.description: The province claims in its lawsuit that the shooting at a rural school “could have been prevented” if OpenAI had shared concerns brewing internally with the police.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Alana Paterson for The New York Times
item.media:description: A makeshift memorial for victims of the mass shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia in February.

item.title: U.S. Strikes on Alleged Drug Boats Could Be Criminal, U.N. Expert Says
item.description: A U.N. human rights investigator, like other experts, concluded that the Trump administration’s deadly attacks violate international law, and said the strikes could be crimes against humanity.
item.dc:creator: Nick Cumming-Bruce
item.category: Human Rights and Human Rights Violations
item.media:description: An image from a video provided by the U.S. military shows a boat moments before it was struck in the eastern Pacific Ocean in April.

item.title: Police Officer Injured in Shooting Near Ontario Synagogue on Yom Kippur
item.description: A gunman opened fire near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville as congregants gathered for Yom Kippur, the authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang and Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
item.media:description: The Sons of Jacob Synagogue, where a police officer outside was shot during a Yom Kippur gathering, in Belleville, Ontario, on Monday.

item.title: U.N. General Assembly to Confront Familiar Crises, New Conflicts and A.I.
item.description: The United Nations is also searching for a replacement for António Guterres, who has served two terms as the secretary general and is stepping down.
item.dc:creator: Farnaz Fassihi
item.category: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
item.media:description: The United Nations headquarters in New York. For the first time, the threat posed by artificial intelligence will be atop the agenda of the U.N. General Assembly meeting this week.

item.title: Where to Find Authentic Argentine Bars and Cafes in Buenos Aires
item.description: These beloved spots are a living mosaic of the Argentine capital’s history and culture. They’re also the perfect places to get an authentic taste of the city.
item.dc:creator: Ruffin Prevost and Agustin Nieto
item.media:description: Bar El Federal, in the San Telmo neighborhood, is one of around 100 establishments that Buenos Aires officially recognizes as “bares notables.”

item.title: Thirty More Arrested in Jovenel Moïse Assassination
item.description: The suspects in the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse include 18 men who were extradited from Haiti to Miami, officials said.
item.dc:creator: David C. Adams
item.media:credit: Adriana Zehbrauskas for The New York Times
item.media:description: A poster showing Haiti’s assassinated president, Jovenel Moïse, in Cap Haitien, Haiti, in 2021.

item.title: On a Dot of France Off Canada, Carney and Macron Talk Partnership

item.dc:creator: Ian Austen

item.title: A Half-Century On, Cycling’s World Championship Returns to Montreal
item.description: Many streets in downtown Montreal and along the south shore of the St. Lawrence River will become a giant sports arena for 1,000 cyclists.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.category: True North: On the Road in Canada (Book)
item.media:description: Since 2010, Montreal and Quebec City have hosted the only two North American races on the International Cycling Union’s World Tour, which includes the Tour de France.

item.title: The Most Handsome Melon in Mexico? Yes, It’s a Real Contest.

item.title: Manitoba Joins List of Canadian Provinces to Stop Changing Clocks
item.description: A survey of 72,000 residents found that most wanted to stop falling back and springing forward every year. The region will now follow others that have abandoned the practice.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel
item.media:credit: Renaud Philippe for The New York Times
item.media:description: A passenger train in Churchill, Manitoba, in 2025. About a third of countries still change their clocks twice a year, though many areas have either considered dropping the practice or taken steps to do so in recent years.

item.title: St. Pierre and Miquelon, France, In the Spotlight as Macron and Carney Visit
item.description: St. Pierre and Miquelon, the French territory off the coast of Canada’s Newfoundland, is experiencing a surge in visitors after three unrelated events raised its profile.
item.dc:creator: Norimitsu Onishi and Renaud Philippe

item.title: Carney Calls for E.U.-Canada Pact Amid ‘Ferocious Storm’
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney told European lawmakers that an alliance would help to secure sovereignty and independence for his country. The moves come amid a historic low for U.S. ties with Canada.

item.title: Trump Sanctions on Cuba Strands Thousands Of Shipping Containers
item.description: The U.S. says its sanctions are not aimed at depriving Cuba of essential goods. Thousands of stranded shipping containers tell a different story.

item.media:description: Ships unloading humanitarian aid at the Port of Havana this year. The challenges in shipping to the island nation are intensifying a humanitarian crisis.

item.title: Living Next to Mexico’s Toxic Reservoir
item.description: Our reporter Emiliano Rodríguez Mega visits the highly polluted Endhó Dam, which some call Mexico’s toilet bowl. People who live nearby say that sickness is everywhere.
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega, Rebecca Suner, Thomas Vollkommer, Joey Sendaydiego and Alejandro Cegarra

item.title: Locals Call It the World’s Largest Cesspool, and Blame It for Surging Cancer
item.description: For decades, the Mexican authorities have sacrificed a rural valley to flush away the capital’s waste and power the economy. Now, local communities are paying for that decision — often with peoples’ lives.
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and Alejandro Cegarra
item.media:credit: Alejandro Cegarra for The New York Times
item.media:description: The old church of San Francisco Bojay in Hidalgo, Mexico, is partially submerged after the area was flooded in 1949 to create the Endhó Dam.

item.title: Oliver Jones, ‘Greatest Living Jazz Musician in Canada,’ Dies at 91

item.media:credit: Stéphane Ouzounoff/Hans Lucas, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
